speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, specifically its appearance and whether it is itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the eyebrows or behind the ears, and have you noticed any crusting or "cradle cap" on the scalp? Are there any other areas of the body affected, such as the diaper area or skin folds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any involvement of the diaper area, and does the rash cause significant itching or discomfort for the infant?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of greasy yellow scales and erythematous patches on the scalp and forehead of a 3-month-old infant, this is consistent with infantile seborrheic dermatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
